question: Each of the \(39\) students in the eighth grade at Lincoln Middle School has one dog or one cat or both a dog and a cat. Twenty students have a dog and \(26\) students have a cat. How many students have both a dog and a cat?
solution:
Adding the dog owners and cat owners gives \(20+26=46\). Every student is included because each has at least one of the two pets. A student with just one pet is counted once, while a student with both pets is counted twice.

Thus the amount by which \(46\) exceeds the actual number of students counts the students with both pets exactly once:
\[
46-39=7.
\]
Therefore \(7\) students have both a dog and a cat, choice \(\mathrm{A}\).
